text.tspan: AKS Automatic → Nexus and on-premises over Azure Virtual WAN (least routable IP space)

Per-environment transit /28 is the only thing connected to the hub. AKS VNets reuse 100.64.0.0/16 and are never advertised. Private clusters, all egress forced through the hub. Validated PoC: westus3, Kubernetes 1.36, Azure Linux 3.
non-routable · reused by every env · never on vWAN

100.64.0.0/16 is never advertised, so the same range can be reused per environment (no overlap on the hub)
Routing intent (Internet) → hub firewall: transit VNets learn 0.0.0.0/0; allow AKS required FQDNs from the transit /28s
• NVA SNAT: Nexus and on-prem only
• All AKS egress uses the NVA + hub;
internet exits only via the hub firewall
breaks, so the ILB drains that instance
(a BGP route beats the peering route)
Limit which pods reach on-prem with
Image pull path and private-CA trust (validated end to end)
kubelet/containerd on node 100.64.1.x resolves nexus.poc.internal (private DNS) → 10.30.0.10
UDR sends 10.30.0.0/24 to the transit ILB 172.19.0.4 (HA ports) → NVA instance
NVA SNATs 100.64.1.x → 172.19.0.x and forwards through the vWAN hub
Nexus NSG admits 443 from the transit /28; nginx presents the cert issued by the private CA
containerd verifies it via AKS custom CA trust (securityProfile.customCATrustCertificates, in the azapi create request)
Gotcha: setting CA trust reimages the hosted system
nodes, but NAP nodes that already exist are NOT
marked drifted and keep failing with x509.
Set it at create time, or recycle NodeClaims

PoC results (westus3, private clusters): pod pull over TLS 326 MB at 1.4–2.2 Gbps · kubelet pull 342 MB in 12.5–13.2 s · pod internet egress IP = hub firewall public IP · before CA trust: ErrImagePull x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
On-prem (simulated with S2S VPN + BGP, 10.40.0.0/24): pod → on-prem server seen as client 172.19.0.6 (NVA) · on-prem learned only 172.19.0.0/28, 10.30.0.0/24 and the hub prefix
Pods that call Nexus themselves must mount the CA (node trust is not injected into containers). Outbound only: on-prem-initiated flows into AKS need a separate design.
